summary: Backend-only iteration 5 for Prescription Reminders. Added /app/backend/tests/test_reminders.py with 20 tests. Parallel (xdist loadscope) full-suite result: 112/114 passed with 2 pre-existing parallel-ordering flakes unrelated to reminders. Serial re-run of both flaky tests → 59/59 PASS. Reminders suite itself: 20/20 PASS in 2.5s. All 10 review-request behaviors verified green: (1) GET /api/reminders on fresh patient → []; (2) POST returns full Reminder object with id, patient_id, kind, title, note, remind_at, completed=false, family_member_id/name null, created_at; (3) POST with valid family_member_id populates family_member_name from DB; (4) POST with foreign family_member_id (from another user's account) → 404; (5) first PATCH toggles completed→true, second PATCH toggles back →false; (6) PATCH unknown id → 404; PATCH another user's reminder → 404 (silent, via query scoped by patient_id); (7) DELETE removes (verified via GET), second DELETE → 404; DELETE another user's reminder → 404; (8) Doctor GET/POST/PATCH/DELETE all rejected with 403; (9) Missing bearer on GET/POST/PATCH/DELETE → 401; invalid bearer → 401; (10) All 4 kinds accepted (refill, follow_up, medication, other). Extra: verified GET returns list sorted by remind_at ASC (matches server sort). No regressions.

minor.issue: server.py:1031-1040 — When rid exists but belongs to another patient, endpoint returns 404 (silent) rather than 403. This is by design (find_one scoped by patient_id) and consistent with DELETE /api/reminders/{id}, but a stricter API might prefer 403 for cross-tenant access on a known resource. Non-blocking; matches spec ('PATCH unknown → 404').
No pagination or filtering (e.g., ?completed=false, ?upcoming=true). Currently caps at 200. Fine for MVP; consider adding query params before scale.

action_items: (Optional) Consider a small refactor to move Reminders + Family + Chat + Files into separate router modules — server.py is now ~1069 lines (well above the 700-line guideline).

(Optional) Address the 2 pre-existing xdist-parallel test flakes (test_doctor_patients_list and test_doctor_get_marks_patient_msg_read) — they occasionally hit a race where the doctor-side fixture runs before the patient fixture has finished seeding data. Same issue was flagged in iteration_4. Suggest scoping those fixtures to 'module' or serializing via @pytest.mark.serial. Not a product bug; only affects parallel test runs.
(Optional) Add a compound index reminders {patient_id: 1, completed: 1, remind_at: 1} once filter query params are introduced.

(Optional) Consider validating that remind_at > now (or at least parseable ISO datetime beyond Pydantic's default) — currently past timestamps are accepted, which is likely intentional but worth confirming.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is now 1069 lines. Reminders block (l.1001-1050) is clean and self-contained — reasonable candidate for extraction into /app/backend/routers/reminders.py alongside other resources.
Reminders CRUD is well-scoped: all mutations use {'id': rid, 'patient_id': user['user_id']} → prevents cross-tenant modification without needing a separate 403 branch (returns 404).

toggle_reminder (l.1031) reads then writes — not atomic. If two clients toggle simultaneously the second may overwrite. Acceptable for a personal reminders feature; could switch to a single findOneAndUpdate with a $bit or $not aggregation pipeline for atomicity.

family_member_name is snapshotted at reminder creation (server.py:1024) — if the family member is later renamed via PATCH /api/family/{id}, the reminder still shows the old name. Same denormalisation pattern is used for appointments and files. Document this or refresh on read if desired.
MongoDB _id is excluded via projection {'_id': 0} on all reminders reads — good.
All timestamps use datetime.now(timezone.utc) via default_factory — timezone-aware, safe for sorting.
The startup index (l.317-318) covers both the list query (patient_id + remind_at sort) and the ownership scope — no additional index tuning needed for current queryset.
Reminder model inherits from ReminderCreate — clean. Response uses response_model=Reminder → Pydantic strips extra fields.
